justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements (R-01, R-02, R-03) are satisfied via Claim Submission UI Module, Adjuster Workspace UI Module, and modular migration mechanisms like Claim Routing Engine and Mainframe Anti-Corruption Layer - ACL.
justifications.performance_efficiency: The sub-2s target against a 5s mainframe (R-05) is met using Claim Caching & Read Model Component, Response Caching Component, asynchronous processing via Azure Service Bus, and ADF parquet staging for batch windows.
justifications.compatibility: Robust coexistence with On-Premises COBOL/DB2 Mainframe is achieved through IBM MQ / CICS Client, Mainframe Integration Adapter, Self-Hosted Integration Runtime (SHIR) Cluster, and Azure Active Directory integration via OIDC/OAuth2.
justifications.usability: Direct user needs are addressed through dedicated UI components in the SPAs container: Claim Submission UI Module for customers/brokers and Adjuster Workspace UI Module for internal claims adjusters.
justifications.reliability: Zero data loss and consistency (R-04) are supported by Outbox Pattern Processor, Duplicate Detection Filter, DLQ Processor / Forwarder, Circuit Breaker & Fallback Manager, and ADF automated reconciliation.
justifications.security: R-07 and security needs are thoroughly addressed via JWT Validation Policy, Azure Active Directory SSO, Database Security & Auditing, Row-Level Security, and Audit Repository Access Component.
justifications.maintainability: Rapid rollback (R-06) and staged migration (R-03) are enabled by Mainframe Message Translator with Versioning & Feature Flags, Claim Routing Engine, and clear isolation via Mainframe Anti-Corruption Layer - ACL.
justifications.portability: The hybrid requirement across on-premises and Azure West Europe is well realized using Azure Container Apps and SHIR, though heavy reliance on proprietary Azure PaaS limits vendor portability.

PERF-01.justification: CQRS read models in Claims Core Service and response caching in APIM decouple adjuster screen queries from synchronous mainframe calls, ensuring sub-2 s screen loads even when mainframe responses lag.
elements: Customer Portal and Adjuster Workspace SPAs
sensitivity_points: Read model cache freshness and hit ratios
tradeoffs: Eventual consistency of cached mainframe data versus immediate UI responsiveness

PERF-02.justification: Peak submissions are buffered by Azure Service Bus and persisted transactionally in Azure SQL Database. Batch replication via Azure Data Factory stages data without exceeding nightly mainframe batch windows.
sensitivity_points: Message queue ingestion throughput and ADF staging capacity
tradeoffs: Asynchronous submission processing versus real-time mainframe confirmation

AVAIL-01.justification: During mainframe downtime, submissions are safely captured in Azure SQL Database and buffered via the Outbox Pattern Processor and Service Bus queues until connectivity resumes after the batch window.
sensitivity_points: Outbox storage retention and circuit breaker reset policies
tradeoffs: Queue depth growth during batch windows versus immediate mainframe synchronization

AVAIL-02.justification: The architecture incorporates Service Bus duplicate detection, transactional outbox processing, ADF reconciliation pipelines, and temporal audit tables, preventing message duplication or data loss during partial sync failures.
sensitivity_points: Idempotency token configuration and duplicate detection time windows
tradeoffs: Overhead of duplicate detection filtering versus risk of double processing

MOD-01.justification: Claim type routing engines, versioned message translators with feature flags, and APIM routing policies allow toggling claim types to the modern engine or rolling back to legacy paths within minutes.
elements: Mainframe Message Translator with Versioning & Feature Flags
sensitivity_points: Feature flag management granularity and routing rule configuration
tradeoffs: Complexity of maintaining dual routing paths versus fast rollback capability

MOD-02.justification: Frontends communicate purely with APIM and Claims Core Service. Decommissioning the mainframe requires only disabling the adapter and ACL layers; customer and adjuster UI modules remain completely unaffected.
elements: Customer Portal and Adjuster Workspace SPAs
sensitivity_points: Strict decoupling of UI contracts from legacy mainframe schemas
tradeoffs: Abstraction overhead via domain models versus zero frontend impact at cutover

SEC-01.justification: Azure AD JWT validation at APIM combined with Azure SQL Row-Level Security restricts cross-broker data access and logs infractions. However, domain-level authorization policy enforcement in the application tier is not fully detailed.
sensitivity_points: Row-level security predicate accuracy and JWT claim propagation
tradeoffs: Database RLS enforcement overhead versus centralized application authorization

SEC-02.justification: Adjusters access claims solely through the modern workspace authenticated against Azure AD, ensuring immediate revocation across all systems. However, existing short-lived JWT bearer tokens may remain valid until expiry unless Continuous Access Evaluation is configured.
elements: Customer Portal and Adjuster Workspace SPAs
sensitivity_points: JWT token time-to-live settings and revocation list synchronization
tradeoffs: Short token lifetimes requiring frequent refreshes versus fast access revocation
